units: Sabb. VI, 1 מ׳ שאינה נקיבה a maḥat without a hole, i.e. a dress or hair-pin; ib. 3 מ׳ הנקובה a needle.

<cite ref="Mishnah Shabbat 1:3">Ib. I, 3</cite> <he>לא יצא החייט במַחֲטוֹ וכ׳</he> the tailor must not go out with his needle near Sabbath eve; ib. 11ᵇ <he>במ׳ התחובה וכ׳</he> with his needle stuck in his garment; Tosef. ib. I, 8.

<cite ref="Mishnah Shabbat 17:2">Sabb. XVII, 2</cite> <he>מ׳ של יד</he> a small (sewing) needle, <he>של סקאיס</he> the sack-needle (for loose and coarse webs); <cite ref="Mishnah Kelim 13:5">Kel. XIII, 5</cite>.
<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Moed Katan 1:8:2">Y. M. Kat. I, 80ᵈ</cite> bot.
<cite ref="Mishnah Orlah 1:4">Orl. I, 4</cite>, v. <cite ref="M01327"><he>מִיתּוּחַ</he></cite>; a. fr.

<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Bava Kamma 10:11:2">Y. B. Kam. X, end, 7ᶜ</cite> <he>מלא מ׳</he> the length of a stitch which those of … interpreted to mean <he>כפליים כמלא מ׳</he> double the length of a stitch; Bar Ḳ. used the expression <he>מלא משיכת המ׳ וכ׳</he> as much as is required for making a stitch (carrying the needle), which R. J. interpreted (<he>כפליים</he>) <he>כמשיכת המ׳</he> double &c.; Bab.

<cite ref="Bava Kamma 119b:13">B. Kam. 119ᵇ</cite> <he>מלא מ׳ וחוץ למ׳ כמלא מ׳</he> the length of a stitch and besides it a thread the length of a stitch (Rashi: the length of a needle).—Pl. <he>מַחֲטִים</he>, <he>מַחֲטִין</he> (m.).
<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Kiddushin 1:1:20">Y. Kidd. I, 58ᶜ</cite> bot.; <cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Shevuot 6:1:3">Y. Shebu. VI, beg. 36ᵈ</cite> <he>שני מ׳</he> two needles (or pins).
Sabb. 96ᵇ תופרי … זורקין מַחֲטֵיהֶן וכ׳ the embroiderers of curtains threw their spools (v. מִיתּוּחַ) one to the other; a. fr.
